text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- While many Finnish citzens are more sceptical than decision-makers about joining EMU in the first wave, 43 percent say that opting out of EMU would hurt to Finland, says a study by the Centre for Business and Policy Studies (EVA).
- Many Finnish candidates for the European Parliament have based their election campaigns on a liberal alcohol policy.
- A growing number of ships dump waste oil into the Baltic Sea and escape punishment.
- Parliament today celebrates the 90th anniversary of Finnish women's right to vote. Finland was the first in Europe to give women the vote.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finland and the European Commission have reached a critical stage in talks towards a compromise on alcohol import quotas.
- Finnish Banks are apprehensive that a newly established import financing fund will not be a success because of insufficent start-up capital.
- Top Labour Ministry civil servant Pertti Sorsa says he would not be surprised if Finnish economic growth were to climb to six percent next year, instead of the predicted four percent.
- Finland had the second highest birth rate in the EU last year, with women giving birth to an average 1.81 children -- second only to Ireland.
DEMARI
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen, speaking at a Social Democratic party meeting, said Finland should pay more attention to what Sweden does than what it says about EMU.
- Finnish Seamen's Union threatening to keep state oil company Neste's ships in port because of pay dispute on two tankers owned by a Neste subsidiary.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Majority of Finns would like to vote on whether to join EMU, Centre for Business and Policy Studies study shows.
- Area codes for phoning to Finland from abroad set to change, with no transition period, on October 12.
AAMULEHTI
- Prices of domestic heating oil hiked in August -- Finnish homeowners can expect bigger heating bills this winter.
